units.title: Livestock Production
units.intro:
Livestock = domesticated animals kept for food, work, fibre or income: cattle, sheep, goats, camels, donkeys, poultry (and a few others). Eritrea’s herd is mostly **extensive / pastoral–agro-pastoral** — animals walk to browse, with extra pressure in the dry season.

Book snapshot of national stock (order-of-magnitude): millions of sheep and goats, substantial cattle and camels, donkeys as the everyday transport animal, very few horses/mules, plus layers such as White Leghorn in more intensive pockets.

1.1.1 Definitions of Livestock and Farm Animals
body: Livestock is defined as “any creature kept for the production of food, wool, skins or fur, or for the purpose of its use in the farming of the land”.
Equines comprise horses, mules and donkeys.
Animal production, or animal husbandry, is the practice of raising animals to obtain products such as meat, milk, eggs, honey and fish (from ponds).
History of livestock: Humans began domesticating animals over 10 000 years ago, beginning with dogs.

cards.title: 1.1.2 Livestock Status and Population in Eritrea
body: In the six zobas of Eritrea, livestock play an important role in the livelihoods of the community and also constitute a key component of the agricultural productive system.
The majority of Eritrea’s livestock are indigenous.
The only exotic breeds introduced in significant numbers are the dairy breed of Holstein-Friesian cattle and the White Leghorn layer chickens.
Several thousand Large White pigs are, however, also found.

cards.title: 1.1.3 Values and Uses of Livestock
body: Describe some of the roles that livestock play in Eritrea.
Livestock play a major role in Eritrean society.
Mixed farming systems where both crops and livestock are kept are common throughout Eritrea.
In these systems livestock are mainly used to plough the land where crops are grown and to provide manure for fertilizing the fields of crops.

cards.title: 1.1.4 Types and Classification of Livestock
body: Livestock are divided into different orders based on the number of toes or hooves they have.
Equines are hindgut fermenters and most digestion takes place in the caecum and the small intestine.
The Bovidae and Camelidae are foregut fermenters, with most digestion taking place in the rumen.
Pigs have a monogastric digestive system that is similar to that of humans.

cards.title: 1.1.5 Breeding and Breeds
body: The caeca are the sites for bacterial fermentation of undigested food material in most non-ruminant livestock.
The colon is the main site of water re-absorption.
Breeding is the mating of a male with a female to obtain a desired type of offspring or progeny.
The latter is called artificial insemination.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The chemical process of cellulose digestion in ruminants is achieved by enzymes produced by which of the following?
cards.why:
**Reasoning**
Ruminant animals do not naturally produce cellulase, the enzyme required to digest cellulose. Cellulase is produced by the symbiotic bacteria, protozoa, and fungi residing within the rumen and reticulum.

**Conclusion**
Thus, cellulose digestion is achieved by **Rumen microorganisms**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following organic elements is found exclusively in proteins and not in carbohydrates or lipids?
cards.why:
**Reasoning**
Carbohydrates and lipids are composed of Carbon, Hydrogen, and Oxygen. Proteins also contain these three elements but additionally contain Nitrogen, which is a key component of amino acids.

**Conclusion**
Therefore, the element found exclusively in proteins is **Nitrogen**.

cards.title: Animal feeds and feeding
body: **Feeds:** roughages (hay, straw, browse) vs concentrates (grain, oil cake). A ration must cover energy, protein, minerals, vitamins and water — water first in Eritrea’s climate.

cards.title: 1.2.1 Feeds and Feed Composition
body: Feed (food) is a material, which, after ingestion by animals, is capable of being digested, absorbed and utilized.
Usually, the term “feed” is used to imply food for livestock.
Food contains materials that can be digested and that cannot be digested.
The components of the food that cannot be digested pass out of the body as faeces and urine.

cards.title: 1.2.2 Common Classifications and Types of Feeds
body: Feed refers to any non-injurious edible material with nutritional value and could be pasture, harvested forages, crop residues, grains or processed animal feeds.
Feeds that have low fibre content (less than 18 per cent) are termed concentrates.
Feeds that have high fibre content (more than 18 per cent) are termed roughages.
As the name indicates, concentrates are dense, whereas roughages are bulky due to the difference in their fibre content.

cards.q: Which of the following stomach compartments is the largest in a newborn calf?

**Conclusion**
Therefore, the largest compartment at birth is the **Abomasum**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: A feedstuff containing more than $$18\%$$ crude fiber and having a low nutrient density is classified as a:
cards.why:
**Reasoning**
By definition, feeds with high fiber content ($$ > 18\%$$ crude fiber) and high bulk, which are lower in digestible nutrients, are classified as roughages (e.g., hay, straw). Concentrates have less than $$18\%$$ fiber.

**Conclusion**
This feedstuff is classified as a **Roughage**.

cards.title: 1.3 Routine management practices
body: Hides and manure used for fertilizer or fuel are also produced from cattle as by-products.
Cattle are divided into two groups, depending on the presence or absence of humps.
The humpless cattle adapted to temperate climatic conditions are called Bos taurus.
Bos taurus cattle are larger in size and therefore consume more feed than other breeds.
Zebus, however, have a greater ability to survive in warmer temperatures and are more resistant to diseases.

cards.title: Routine management practices
body: **Routine management:** identification, castration / culling, vaccination and deworming, milking hygiene, housing that is dry and ventilated, mating at the right weight (book example: a 25–30 kg doe, breed around 19–23 kg). Extensive cattle grow slowly; better feeding shortens time to market.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The system of feeding where green forage is cut at an optimum growth stage and carried to animals in confinement is called:
cards.why:
**Reasoning**
Zero grazing, also referred to as the cut-and-carry method, involves harvesting the forage fresh from the field and feeding it to housed animals, preventing pasture damage and energy loss from movement.

**Conclusion**
This feeding management system is **Zero grazing**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The humped cattle native to Eritrea, such as the Barka and Arado breeds, belong to which zoological species?
cards.why:
**Reasoning**
Humped cattle, also known as Zebu cattle, belong to the species *Bos indicus*. They are well-adapted to warm tropical temperatures and are resistant to local diseases. Humpless cattle belong to *Bos taurus*.

**Conclusion**
Therefore, these humped breeds belong to **Bos indicus**.

cards.title: 1.4 Animal housing and equipment
body: Housing also makes it easier to detect a number of disease symptoms such as diarrhoea, and to check and apply medication for external parasites such as ticks.
The owner can choose whatever fits him or her for a particular situation.
The structure has to be a place where animals can live, eat and rest comfortably.
The farmer has to be able to work there with ease.
Dairy cows can be housed in one stall but then require separate partitions for milking cows, the bull, heifers and calves.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which hormone is responsible for milk let-down in dairy cows, stimulated by washing the udder with warm water?
cards.why:
**Reasoning**
Washing the udder with warm water sends sensory nerve impulses to the brain, triggering the pituitary gland to release oxytocin into the bloodstream. This hormone causes contraction of the alveoli, forcing milk down into the teats.

**Conclusion**
Thus, the milk let-down hormone is **Oxytocin**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which tool is commonly used to perform closed (bloodless) castration in farm animals by crushing the spermatic cords?
cards.why:
**Reasoning**
The Burdizzo castrator (emasculatome) is designed to crush the spermatic cord and blood vessels leading to the testicles without cutting the scrotum skin. This cuts off the blood supply, causing the testicle to atrophy.

**Conclusion**
Therefore, the tool used for bloodless crushing is the **Burdizzo castrator**.

cards.title: Animal health
body: **Health:** prevent more than cure — quarantine new animals, vaccinate, control ticks and flukes, bury or burn carcasses, keep houses clean. Common groups: bacterial, viral, parasitic (ticks, worms, flukes).

cards.title: 1.5.1 Common Diseases and Parasites Affecting Livestock
body: Causes of diseases can be infectious and non-infectious.
Causes of infectious diseases can be bacterial, viral, fungal and parasitic (internal and external parasites).
The disease is caused by a bacterium known as Mycobacterium bovis (M.bovis).
The main source of infection is the diseased animal itself.

cards.title: 1.5.2 Prevention and Control Measures for Common Diseases and Parasites
body: Describe some of the methods whereby diseases are controlled and eradicated.
Prevention of diseases is much more effective and cheaper than cure.
Appropriate preventive programmes have to be designed and implemented.
For animals to be healthy, they have to be well nourished, and provided with adequate water.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: An adult female sheep is zoologically referred to as a(n):
cards.why:
**Reasoning**
Based on standardized animal science terminology: an adult female sheep is an ewe; an adult female goat is a doe; an adult female pig is a sow; and a young female cow is a heifer.

**Conclusion**
Therefore, the correct term is **Ewe**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following poultry breeds is a specialized egg-layer introduced to increase egg production?
cards.why:
**Reasoning**
The White Leghorn is an exotic breed specialized for high egg-laying capacity (up to $$270\text{ eggs/year}$$). Rhode Island Red is dual-purpose, Fayoumi is intermediate, and Large White is a pig breed.

**Conclusion**
The specialized egg-layer is the **White Leghorn**.

glossary.meaning: Livestock is defined as “any creature kept for the production of food, wool, skins or fur, or for the purpose of its use in the farming of the land”.
Cellulose is a complex carbohydrate found in the cell walls of all plants.
Pigs are the farm animals that have the closest digestive system to that of humans.
Breeding is the mating of a male with a female to obtain a desired type of offspring or progeny.
Culling is the practice of removing animals with undesirable characteristics or traits.
Inbreeding is the mating of related animals of the same breed and it includes close-breeding and linebreeding.
Carbohydrates are the nutrients that serve as the major source of energy for all domestic animals.
Starch is the form of energy stored in plants and found in cereal grains and tubers.
Lipids are a highly concentrated source of energy.
Mastitis is the inflammation of the udder.
Control measures are the destruction of grass mites in pasture by ploughing and planting suitable crops.
Antiseptic is an agent that controls or kills micro-organisms.
Inoculation is the process whereby antiserum is administered to an animal.

tips.text: Farm animals such as cattle, sheep, goats and poultry provide valuable products such as meat, milk and eggs.
Equines (horses, mules and donkeys) provide draught power to plough land and transport people and goods.
Livestock provide manure used for fertilizer or fuel and play a social role in the community.
Domestication of animals was a major event in the history of humankind in that it ensured a steady supply of food and contributed to the division of labour.
Livestock are divided into ruminants and non-ruminants (monogastric animals) based on their digestive system.
Ruminants are cattle, sheep and goats while non-ruminants include poultry and pigs.
The aim of breeding livestock should be to improve the genetic make up of the next generation. This can be done by selection and cross-breeding.
